title: Returned artifact URL is built from the incoming request base URL
reasoning: The upload response constructs the artifact URL directly from request.base_url. In common ASGI deployments, that value can depend on Host or forwarded headers unless separately constrained by trusted-host/proxy middleware. A malicious or misconfigured inbound host can therefore cause the API to return an attacker-chosen absolute artifact URL, which is risky if clients persist, display, or later fetch the returned URL as authoritative.
reproduction: POST /api/artifacts/ with a forged Host header in a deployment that does not enforce trusted hosts; the response url field will use that host.
recommendation: Build artifact URLs from a configured public base URL, or return a relative path such as /api/artifacts/{artifact_id}. If request-derived hosts are required, ensure trusted host/proxy middleware is enforced and add a test for the expected base URL behavior.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No linked tests were included for response URL construction, and the handler has no local guard showing the request host has been validated.
suggestedRegressionTest: Add a route test that sends a forged Host header and asserts the returned url uses the configured public base URL or remains relative.
minimumFixScope: backend/src/api/routes/artifacts/router.py and configuration/test coverage for artifact URL generation.
